title: React context composition state ownership and component architecture
concepts: Component architecture begins by dividing a UI into components and composing them through explicit inputs and nested content.
State should be owned by the lowest component that needs to coordinate its consumers. Keep independent state local; lift shared state to the closest common parent.
Controlled components receive important values and callbacks from a parent; uncontrolled components keep their own local state. Many designs combine both patterns.

A good state shape groups values that change together while avoiding contradictory, redundant, duplicated, and deeply nested data. Values derivable from props or state should usually be calculated during render.
Context is an alternative for values needed by distant descendants. It removes pass-through props, but makes data flow less explicit and can broaden the set of consumers affected by updates.
Composition lets a parent supply JSX as children or named content so intermediate components need not know the details of the content they wrap.

Reducers can centralize complex transitions, while external state libraries add their own store, subscription, derivation, and side-effect conventions; choose them in response to actual coordination needs.
